mainTopic: Three מחלוקות of רבי יוחנן and ריש לקיש about a מנחה: mixing outside the עזרה, a shortage before קמיצה, and shrunken שירים
overview: The amud opens by finishing a question on רבי יוחנן's rule that the less holy place cannot be stricter than the holier one. The גמרא asks why a פסוק is needed to allow eating קדשי קדשים in the היכל. It answers that serving in your master's place is respectful, but eating there is not, so eating needs an explicit פסוק. Next, רבי יוחנן and ריש לקיש argue about a מנחה whose oil was mixed in outside the עזרה. ריש לקיש says that since no כהן is needed for mixing, being inside is not needed either. רבי יוחנן says that because it is made in a holy כלי, it must be done inside, and a ברייתא supports him. Then they argue about a מנחה that became short before קמיצה, and ריש לקיש is refuted from the oil of a מצורע. Finally they argue about שירים that shrank before the קומץ was burned. Both agree according to רבי אליעזר. רבי יוחנן reads רבי יהושע as strict only when nothing at all is left, and he proves this from a ברייתא about זבחים.

steps.title: The verse that permits eating in the most holy place
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the פסוק 'בקדש הקדשים תאכלנו' as the basis for the question that comes next.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'In the most holy place you shall eat it.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes a פסוק saying כהנים may eat the most holy offerings in the 'most holy place'. This is setting up the question in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Normally קדשי קדשים are eaten in the courtyard, the עזרה. This פסוק adds that they may also be eaten in the holier area, the היכל. The גמרא is about to ask why this needed to be written at all.

keyTerms.meaning: The most holy place. Here it is understood as the היכל, the Sanctuary building itself.
You shall eat it.

phrases.english: "In the most holy place you shall eat it."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the earlier discussion of רבי יוחנן's rule about doing things inside the היכל.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A פסוק explicitly permits eating קדשי קדשים in the היכל.

steps.title: Why is a verse needed if the lesser area can't be stricter?
steps.stepSummary: If eating is allowed in the courtyard, the היכל should be allowed automatically by the rule 'לא יהא טפל חמור מן העיקר'. So why write a פסוק?
steps.simpleTranslation: Why do I need a verse? Let us say: 'In the courtyard of the אהל מועד they shall eat it,' and the minor place should not be stricter than the main one.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רבי יוחנן's rule. If that rule is true, the פסוק about eating in the היכל seems unnecessary.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יוחנן said the courtyard, the 'minor' place, cannot be stricter than the היכל, the 'main' holy place. If so, eating permitted in the courtyard should be permitted in the היכל by logic alone. An extra פסוק suggests that logic doesn't work.

keyTerms.meaning: Why do I need a verse? Used when something seems to be known already.
The secondary or lesser thing. Here, the courtyard.
The main thing. Here, the היכל.

keyTerms.term: לֹא יְהֵא טָפֵל חָמוּר מִן הָעִיקָּר
keyTerms.meaning: The lesser should not be stricter than the main.

steps.confusionAlert: Don't mix up the two places. The courtyard (עזרה) is the 'טפל', the less holy place. The היכל is the 'עיקר', the holier place. The logic is: if it's allowed in the less holy place, surely it's allowed in the holier one.

phrases.english: But why do I need this verse?
Let him say: "In the courtyard of the Tent of Meeting they shall eat it,"
and the minor should not be more stringent
than the main one.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Uses the פסוק from step 1 to attack רבי יוחנן's rule.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי יוחנן's rule that the היכל is never stricter than the courtyard.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If the rule were true, the פסוק permitting eating in the היכל would be unnecessary.

steps.title: Serving in the master's place differs from eating there
steps.stepSummary: The rule works for עבודה, because serving in the master's place is fine. It does not work for eating, because eating in the master's place is disrespectful. So eating in the היכל needs a פסוק.
steps.simpleTranslation: For service, where a person serves in his master's place, we say the minor should not be stricter than the main. For eating, where a person does not eat in his master's place, it is allowed only because the verse wrote it. Had the verse not written it, we would not apply the rule.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers: the rule applies to service, like שחיטה, but not to eating. So the פסוק is needed for eating.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Serving your master right where he is shows respect, so the היכל can't be stricter for עבודה. Eating in front of your master is disrespectful, so logic alone would never permit eating in the היכל. That is why the פסוק had to say it, and רבי יוחנן's rule still stands for עבודה.

keyTerms.meaning: The Temple service, such as שחיטה.
Eating the offering.
In his master's place.
The reason is that the verse wrote it, meaning only because of the פסוק.

steps.whatToRemember: The rule 'לא יהא טפל חמור מן העיקר' works for עבודה but not for אכילה. Serving in the master's place is respectful; eating there is not.

phrases.english: Service, where a person serves in his master's place,
we say that the minor should not be
more stringent than the main one.

phrases.aramaic: אֲכִילָה, שֶׁאֵין אָדָם אוֹכֵל בִּמְקוֹם רַבּוֹ,
phrases.english: Eating, where a person does not eat in his master's place,
the reason it is allowed is that the verse wrote it;
but if the verse had not written it,

phrases.aramaic: לֹא יְהֵא טָפֵל חָמוּר מִן הָעִיקָּר
phrases.english: 'the minor should not be more stringent than the main'
we would not say.

steps.terutzResolutionType: Distinction between two kinds of acts (service vs. eating).
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The rule should apply to everything done in the courtyard, including eating, so the פסוק is extra.
steps.terutzMaskana: The rule applies only to עבודה. Eating in the master's place is disrespectful, so it needs an explicit פסוק.

steps.title: Mixing a meal offering's oil outside the courtyard
steps.stepSummary: A new topic: if the oil of a מנחה was mixed in outside the עזרה, רבי יוחנן says it is פסולה and ריש לקיש says it is כשרה.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was stated: if he mixed it outside the wall of the courtyard, רבי יוחנן says it is disqualified, and ריש לקיש says it is valid.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens a new מחלוקת. Is a מנחה still valid if the oil was mixed in outside the עזרה?
steps.deeperAnalysis: בלילה is mixing the oil into the flour of the מנחה. רבי יוחנן holds it must be done inside the עזרה, or the מנחה is פסולה. ריש לקיש holds that doing it outside does not ruin it.

keyTerms.meaning: He mixed it, meaning mixing the oil into the flour of the מנחה.
The wall of the Temple courtyard.
Disqualified.
Valid.

phrases.english: It was stated:
If he mixed it outside the wall of the courtyard,
phrases.notes: 'It' is a מנחה, a meal offering; he mixed its oil into the flour.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yoḥanan says: it is disqualified;
Reish Lakish says: it is valid.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic, unrelated to the previous back-and-forth.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: מחלוקת: רבי יוחנן says mixing outside the עזרה makes the מנחה פסולה; ריש לקיש says it is כשרה.

steps.title: ריש לקיש's proof from the order of the verses
steps.stepSummary: ריש לקיש brings his source. The תורה first mentions pouring oil and putting לבונה, and only afterward bringing the מנחה to the כהנים. So the כהנים are not yet involved at the oil stage. The next step draws the conclusion.
steps.simpleTranslation: ריש לקיש says it is valid, as it is written: 'And he shall pour oil upon it and put frankincense upon it,' and then: 'And he shall bring it to the sons of אהרן the כהנים, and he shall take a handful.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings ריש לקיש's source. The order of the פסוקים shows that the oil is handled before the מנחה is brought to the כהנים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Pouring the oil comes first in the פסוק. Only afterward does the מנחה get brought to the כהנים, and then the קמיצה is done. This order will show that the oil work does not need a כהן. From that, in the next step, ריש לקיש concludes it does not need to be inside the עזרה either.

keyTerms.meaning: And he shall pour.
Frankincense, placed on the מנחה.
And afterward. It points to the order of the פסוקים.
And he shall take a handful. This is the קמיצה, done by the כהן.

steps.whyThisMatters: This shows a common way to learn הלכה: the order of steps in the פסוק tells us which steps need a כהן and which do not. Whether that also decides where a step must be done is exactly what רבי יוחנן disputes in step 7.

phrases.english: Reish Lakish says it is valid,
as it is written: "And he shall pour oil upon it
and put frankincense upon it,"
and afterward: "And he shall bring it to the sons of Aaron,
the priests, and he shall take a handful."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the source for ריש לקיש's view from step 4.
steps.raayaObject: ריש לקיש's ruling that a מנחה mixed outside the עזרה is כשרה.
steps.raayaSupportSource: ויקרא 2:1-2: pouring oil and putting לבונה come before bringing the מנחה to the כהנים.

steps.title: ריש לקיש finishes his proof: no priest needed, so no courtyard needed
steps.stepSummary: ריש לקיש completes his proof. The כהונה part only starts at קמיצה, so pouring and mixing can be done by a זר. If a כהן is not needed, being inside the עזרה is not needed either.
steps.simpleTranslation: From the taking of the handful onward, it is a job for כהנים. This teaches that pouring and mixing are valid even when done by a non-כהן. And since a כהן is not needed, being inside the עזרה is also not needed.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is finishing ריש לקיש's proof from step 5. He draws the conclusion that mixing outside the עזרה is allowed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק only brings the כהנים into the picture at קמיצה. So pouring and mixing, which come earlier, do not need a כהן. ריש לקיש then reasons that a step which does not need a כהן also does not need to be done in the holy area.

keyTerms.meaning: The כהן taking a handful of the מנחה to burn on the מזבח
Pouring the oil onto the flour
Mixing the oil into the flour
A non-כהן
Inside, meaning inside the עזרה

phrases.english: From the taking of the handful onward, it is a מצוה of the priesthood,
this taught about pouring and mixing
that they are valid when done by a non-priest.
And since priesthood is not required,
inside is also not required.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the proof begun in step 5 by drawing the legal inference.
steps.raayaObject: ריש לקיש's view that a מנחה mixed outside the עזרה is כשרה
steps.raayaSupportSource: The order of the פסוקים: pouring and mixing come before the מנחה is brought to the כהנים, and קמיצה comes after.

steps.title: רבי יוחנן's reason: it is made in a holy vessel
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן says the מנחה is פסולה. It is prepared in a holy כלי, so even if a כהן is not needed, it still must be done inside the עזרה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוחנן says it is invalid. Since the מנחה is made in a holy vessel, a כהן may not be needed, but it at least needs to be done inside.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives רבי יוחנן's reason for saying the מנחה is פסולה. He blocks ריש לקיש's jump from 'no כהן needed' to 'no inside needed.'
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יוחנן agrees that a זר may mix. But he says 'who does it' and 'where it is done' are separate questions. Because the mixing happens in a holy כלי שרת, it belongs inside the עזרה.

keyTerms.meaning: Invalid, disqualified
Its preparation is done in a holy vessel
Granted that, even if
At least, in any case

phrases.english: And Rabbi Yochanan says: It is invalid,
since its preparation is in a vessel,
phrases.notes: He means a כלי שרת, a holy vessel used in the מקדש.

phrases.english: granted that priesthood is not required,
being inside, at least, is required.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives רבי יוחנן's reasoning and breaks the link ריש לקיש made between needing a כהן and needing to be inside.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A מנחה mixed outside the עזרה is פסולה, because its preparation in a holy כלי requires it to be inside, even though a זר may do it.

steps.title: A ברייתא supports רבי יוחנן
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא says a זר who mixed the מנחה leaves it כשרה, but mixing outside the עזרה makes it פסולה. This matches רבי יוחנן exactly.
steps.simpleTranslation: A ברייתא was taught that agrees with רבי יוחנן: if a non-כהן mixed it, it is valid. If it was mixed outside the wall of the עזרה, it is invalid.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא that supports רבי יוחנן's view.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא separates the two questions just like רבי יוחנן did. A זר is fine, but outside is not. This shows that 'no כהן needed' does not mean 'no inside needed,' against ריש לקיש's reasoning.

keyTerms.meaning: He mixed it
Valid
The wall of the Temple courtyard

steps.whatToRemember: Mixing the oil may be done by a זר, but according to רבי יוחנן and the ברייתא it must be done inside the עזרה.

phrases.english: It is taught in a baraita in accordance with Rabbi Yochanan:
If a non-priest mixed it, it is valid;
if it was mixed outside the wall of the courtyard, it is invalid.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports the view given in step 7 with a תנאי source.
steps.raayaObject: רבי יוחנן's view that mixing outside the עזרה makes the מנחה פסולה
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא: בלל זר is כשרה, but outside the wall of the עזרה it is פסולה.

steps.title: New dispute: a meal offering that became short before the handful
steps.stepSummary: A new מחלוקת. If a מנחה lost some of its flour before קמיצה, רבי יוחנן says the owner may bring more from home to fill it. ריש לקיש says he may not.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was stated: a מנחה that became short before the taking of the handful. רבי יוחנן says he may bring flour from his house and fill it up. ריש לקיש says he may not bring flour from his house and fill it up.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens a new מחלוקת between רבי יוחנן and ריש לקיש about a מנחה that is missing some flour.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The case is a מנחה that has less than its required amount, and the shortage happened before קמיצה. The question is whether it can be repaired by adding flour, or whether it is ruined and a new מנחה is needed.

keyTerms.meaning: Became short, lost some of its amount
Before the handful was taken
From his house, meaning ordinary unsanctified flour
And fill it up to its full amount

steps.confusionAlert: In the last מחלוקת רבי יוחנן was the strict one. Here it flips: רבי יוחנן is lenient and lets the owner fix it, and ריש לקיש is strict.

phrases.english: It was stated: A meal offering that became lacking before the taking of the handful,
Rabbi Yochanan says:
He shall bring from within his house and fill it;
Reish Lakish says:
He shall not bring from within his house and fill it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic with the same two אמוראים.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי יוחנן: a מנחה that became short before קמיצה can be filled from home. ריש לקיש: it cannot.

steps.title: The reasons: the handful fixes it, or the holy vessel fixes it
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא repeats both opinions and adds the reason for each. For רבי יוחנן, only קמיצה fixes the מנחה. For ריש לקיש, being put in a holy כלי already fixes it.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוחנן says he brings flour from his house and fills it, because the קמיצה is what fixes it. ריש לקיש says he may not bring flour from his house and fill it, because the holiness of the vessel is what fixes it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא repeats the two opinions, this time to explain the reason behind each one.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both agree that once a מנחה is 'fixed,' losing flour ruins it. They argue about what fixes it. רבי יוחנן says the קמיצה does, so before קמיצה it can still be filled. ריש לקיש says the holy כלי does, so once it is in the כלי, a shortage cannot be repaired.

keyTerms.meaning: Fixes it, sets its status as a finished מנחה
The holiness given by a כלי שרת

steps.whatToRemember: רבי יוחנן: קמיצה fixes the מנחה, so before it a shortage can be filled. ריש לקיש: the holy כלי fixes it, so after it goes into the כלי it cannot be filled.
steps.whyThisMatters: This shows the real argument underneath: which moment makes a מנחה 'locked in.' That decides when a shortage becomes a פסול.

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן אָמַר: מֵבִיא מִתּוֹךְ בֵּיתוֹ וִימַלְּאֶנָּה,
phrases.english: Rabbi Yochanan says: He brings from within his house and fills it,
because the taking of the handful fixes it.

phrases.aramaic: רֵישׁ לָקִישׁ אָמַר: לָא יָבִיא מִתּוֹךְ בֵּיתוֹ וִימַלְּאֶנָּה,
phrases.english: Reish Lakish says: He shall not bring from within his house and fill it,
because the sanctity of the vessel fixes it.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן אָמַר: מֵבִיא מִתּוֹךְ בֵּיתוֹ וִימַלְּאֶנָּה, קְמִיצָה קָבְעָה לֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Restates the מחלוקת from step 9 in order to give the reason behind each side.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי יוחנן: קמיצה fixes the מנחה's status. ריש לקיש: the holiness of the כלי fixes it.

steps.title: רבי יוחנן refutes ריש לקיש from the oil of a מצורע
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן challenges ריש לקיש with a משנה about the לוג of oil of a מצורע: if it became short before pouring, it may be refilled. The גמרא says this is a full refutation.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוחנן challenged ריש לקיש: if the לוג of oil became short before the כהן poured from it, he should fill it up. This is a refutation of ריש לקיש.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוחנן attacks ריש לקיש's view from Step 10 using a משנה, and the גמרא admits ריש לקיש is refuted.
steps.deeperAnalysis: ריש לקיש said that once something is put into a holy כלי, it is fixed and can no longer be topped up. But the משנה says the מצורע's oil, which is already in a holy כלי, may still be refilled before pouring. So being in a holy כלי does not lock it in, just as רבי יוחנן said.

keyTerms.meaning: A measure of liquid; here, the oil a מצורע brings for his purification
He poured (the כהן pouring oil into his palm)
He should fill it up
A full refutation; the view is rejected

steps.whatToRemember: The מחלוקת about a מנחה that became short before קמיצה ends with ריש לקיש refuted. The holy כלי alone does not stop you from topping up. Only קמיצה does.

phrases.aramaic: אֵיתִיבֵיהּ רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן לְרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן לָקִישׁ:
phrases.english: Rabbi Yochanan challenged Rabbi Shimon ben Lakish:
If the log of oil became short,
phrases.notes: This is a quote from a משנה in נגעים about the oil a מצורע brings.

phrases.english: if it happened before he poured, he should fill it up.
This is a refutation.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֵיתִיבֵיהּ רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן לְרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן לָקִישׁ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks ריש לקיש's reason given in Step 10
steps.kashyaTarget: ריש לקיש's rule that a holy כלי already fixes the amount
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The מצורע's oil is in a holy כלי, yet the משנה lets it be refilled. So the holy כלי does not lock in the amount.

steps.title: New argument: the leftover shrank between קמיצה and burning
steps.stepSummary: A new מחלוקת: the שירים of a מנחה became less after קמיצה but before the קומץ was burned. רבי יוחנן says the קומץ is still burned for them. ריש לקיש says it is not.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was stated: if the leftover became short between קמיצה and burning, רבי יוחנן says the קומץ is burned for it, and ריש לקיש says it is not.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens a brand-new מחלוקת between the same two אמוראים. This time the flour went missing after קמיצה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Burning the קומץ is what lets the כהנים eat the שירים. The question is whether shrunken שירים are still good enough for the קומץ to be burned for them. רבי יוחנן says yes; ריש לקיש says no.

keyTerms.meaning: The leftover of the מנחה after the handful is taken; the כהנים eat it
Burning on the מזבח
The handful of the מנחה that gets burned
He burns (the קומץ) for them, so they become permitted to eat

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix this up with Steps 9-10. There the flour went missing before קמיצה, and the question was refilling. Here it went missing after קמיצה, and the question is whether the קומץ can still be burned.

phrases.english: It was stated:
A leftover that became short
between the taking of the handful and the burning,

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן אָמַר: מַקְטִיר קוֹמֶץ עֲלֵיהֶן,
phrases.english: Rabbi Yochanan says: he burns the handful for them,

phrases.aramaic: וְרֵישׁ לָקִישׁ אָמַר: אֵין מַקְטִיר קוֹמֶץ עֲלֵיהֶן.
phrases.english: and Reish Lakish says: he does not burn the handful for them.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִיתְּמַר: שִׁירַיִם שֶׁחָסְרוּ בֵּין קְמִיצָה לְהַקְטָרָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new מחלוקת after the dispute about a short מנחה (steps 9-11) ended in a refutation of ריש לקיש
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי יוחנן: burn the קומץ for shrunken שירים. ריש לקיש: do not.

steps.title: The argument is only according to רבי יהושע
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא narrows the מחלוקת. According to רבי אליעזר, both agree the קומץ is burned. They only argue about what רבי יהושע would hold.
steps.simpleTranslation: According to רבי אליעזר, everyone agrees. They argue only about what רבי יהושע holds.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pins down exactly where the argument is. This sets up the next step, which brings the משנה where רבי אליעזר and רבי יהושע argue.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי אליעזר is lenient even when the שירים are completely gone, so shrunken שירים are surely fine for him. The real question is רבי יהושע, who is stricter.

keyTerms.meaning: According to the view of
Everyone agrees; there is no argument
Where they do argue

phrases.english: According to Rabbi Eliezer
everyone agrees,
where they argue is according to Rabbi Yehoshua.

steps.triggerLanguage: אַלִּיבָּא דְּרַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר כּוּלֵּי עָלְמָא לָא פְּלִיגִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Narrows the מחלוקת of Step 12 to one תנא's view
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Both אמוראים agree according to רבי אליעזר. They argue only about רבי יהושע.

steps.title: The משנה where רבי אליעזר and רבי יהושע argue
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה. If the שירים became impure, were burned, or were lost, רבי אליעזר says the מנחה is valid and רבי יהושע says it is invalid.
steps.simpleTranslation: As we learned: if its leftover became impure, was burned, or was lost, by רבי אליעזר's approach it is valid, and by רבי יהושע's approach it is invalid.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings the משנה that shows the argument between רבי אליעזר and רבי יהושע that Step 13 mentioned.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For רבי אליעזר, the קומץ can be burned even with no שירים left to eat. For רבי יהושע, it cannot. This is the base the two אמוראים are working from.

keyTerms.meaning: Became ritually impure
Were lost
According to the approach (way of thinking) of
Valid / invalid

phrases.english: As we learned in a mishna:
If its leftover became impure,
its leftover was burned, or its leftover was lost —
by the approach of Rabbi Eliezer it is valid,
by the approach of Rabbi Yehoshua it is invalid.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supplies the source for the תנאים mentioned in Step 13
steps.raayaObject: That רבי אליעזר and רבי יהושע argue about a מנחה whose שירים are gone

steps.title: How each אמורא reads רבי יהושע
steps.stepSummary: ריש לקיש, who says the מנחה is invalid, simply follows רבי יהושע. רבי יוחנן says רבי יהושע was strict only when nothing was left. If some שירים remain, even רבי יהושע agrees the קומץ is burned.
steps.simpleTranslation: The one who says invalid follows רבי יהושע. The one who says valid says: רבי יהושע only said this where nothing was left. But where something was left, even רבי יהושע agrees.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains how each side of the new מחלוקת fits with רבי יהושע.
steps.deeperAnalysis: ריש לקיש takes רבי יהושע's strictness to cover any loss of the שירים, even a partial one. רבי יוחנן limits it to a case where the שירים are totally gone. If even a little remains, there is still something for the קומץ to permit, so it may be burned.

keyTerms.meaning: The one who rules it invalid
The one who rules it valid
He only said it (in that case), meaning his ruling is limited
Something remained
Agrees

steps.whatToRemember: Shrunken שירים: ריש לקיש reads רבי יהושע broadly (invalid). רבי יוחנן reads him narrowly: invalid only if nothing is left. So if something is left, the קומץ is still burned.
steps.whyThisMatters: This is a classic גמרא move. Both אמוראים accept the same תנא, but they argue about how far his ruling reaches.

phrases.english: The one who invalidates holds like Rabbi Yehoshua,
and the one who validates says:

phrases.aramaic: עַד כָּאן לֹא אָמַר רַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ הָתָם
phrases.english: Rabbi Yehoshua only said it there,
where nothing remained,
but where something remained,
even Rabbi Yehoshua agrees with him.
phrases.notes: "Him" is רבי אליעזר, who says the מנחה is valid.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאן דְּפָסֵל – כְּרַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ, וּמַאן דְּמַכְשַׁר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Applies the משנה of Step 14 to the two sides of Step 12
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: ריש לקיש follows רבי יהושע plainly. רבי יוחנן limits רבי יהושע to a case where no שירים are left, so partly remaining שירים still allow the קומץ to be burned.

steps.title: If a כזית of a זבח is left, the blood is still sprinkled
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes a ברייתא in which רבי יהושע rules that if a כזית of meat or fat is left from any זבח, the כהן sprinkles the blood. With less than a כזית, he does not.
steps.simpleTranslation: As a ברייתא teaches: רבי יהושע says, for any offering in the תורה, if a כזית of meat or a כזית of fat is left, the כהן sprinkles the blood. If only half a כזית of meat and half a כזית of fat are left, he does not sprinkle the blood.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא to prove רבי יוחנן right. רבי יהושע is not strict when part of the קרבן is still there.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Even though most of the animal is gone, a single כזית left over is enough for זריקת הדם. That fits רבי יוחנן's claim that רבי יהושע was strict only when nothing at all was left. Two halves, one of meat and one of fat, do not join together, because the meat is eaten and the fat is burned. They are two different uses.

keyTerms.meaning: Animal offerings
An olive-sized amount, the smallest amount that counts in halacha
The meat of the קרבן, which is eaten
The fats of the קרבן, which are burned on the מזבח
Sprinkling the blood on the מזבח, the key act that makes the קרבן work

steps.confusionAlert: Half a כזית of meat plus half a כזית of fat does NOT add up to one כזית here. The meat and the fat have different jobs, so they cannot be counted together.

phrases.english: As it is taught: Rabbi Yehoshua says:
All the offerings that are in the Torah
from which an olive-bulk of meat was left over
or an olive-bulk of fat – he sprinkles the blood,
phrases.notes: The rest of the animal was lost or became impure, and only this small amount is still there.

phrases.aramaic: כַּחֲצִי זַיִת בָּשָׂר כַּחֲצִי זַיִת חֵלֶב –
phrases.english: half an olive-bulk of meat and half an olive-bulk of fat –
he does not sprinkle the blood.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports רבי יוחנן's claim in Step 15 that רבי יהושע allows the service when something remains.
steps.raayaObject: רבי יוחנן's claim that רבי יהושע invalidates only when nothing remains
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא of רבי יהושע: a כזית left over from a זבח still allows זריקת הדם

steps.title: An עולה counts even with two halves, but a מנחה does not count
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא continues. With an עולה, half a כזית of meat and half a כזית of fat are enough, because all of it is burned. A מנחה does not count toward what is left, even if it is fully there.
steps.simpleTranslation: With an עולה, even if only half a כזית of meat and half a כזית of fat are left, the כהן sprinkles the blood, because an עולה is burned completely. But with the מנחה, even if it is all still there, he should not sprinkle.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא adds two more cases. In an עולה, the halves do join together. A מנחה does not help the animal's blood get sprinkled.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In an עולה, the meat and the fat both go on the מזבח. Since they have the same job, the two halves join into one כזית. The מנחה brought along with the animal is not part of the animal itself. So even a whole מנחה does not count as "something left" of the זבח.

keyTerms.meaning: A burnt offering, which is burned completely on the מזבח
Completely burned, with nothing eaten
A flour offering
Still there, intact

steps.whatToRemember: רבי יהושע lets the service continue as long as a real, countable part of the קרבן itself is left. This backs up רבי יוחנן: if some שירים of a מנחה remain, even רבי יהושע would burn the קומץ.

phrases.english: And with a burnt offering, even half an olive-bulk of meat

phrases.aramaic: וְכַחֲצִי זַיִת חֵלֶב – זוֹרֵק אֶת הַדָּם,
phrases.english: and half an olive-bulk of fat – he sprinkles the blood,
because a burnt offering is entirely burned,
phrases.notes: Since the meat and the fat both go on the מזבח, the two halves join to make one כזית.

phrases.aramaic: וּבַמִּנְחָה, אַף עַל פִּי שֶׁכּוּלָּהּ קַיֶּימֶת –
phrases.english: and with the meal offering, even though all of it is intact –
phrases.notes: This is the flour offering brought along with the animal. Even if all of it is there, it doesn't count as part of the animal.

phrases.english: he shall not sprinkle.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the same ברייתא with the special case of an עולה and the limit set by the מנחה.
steps.raayaObject: רבי יוחנן's view of רבי יהושע
steps.raayaSupportSource: The rest of רבי יהושע's ברייתא: an עולה counts even with two halves, but a separate מנחה does not count
